answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to forge a verifiable work history before it earns trust: new identities start with tiny transaction limits and only gain larger quotas after a history of honest, attested work accumulates, like water slowly carving karst caves rather than flooding in at once. Reputation then acts as nectar — valuable, earned slowly, and costly to fake at scale — so creating thousands of throwaway identities yields no shortcut to influence, because each one must independently pay the same time and proof cost.
